summary: Architecture for changeset-aware `make test` using a static reverse import graph (grimp) keyed off a per-branch gitignored last-known-good (LKG) sidecar. Computes the diff from the best available baseline (LKG if present and reachable, else `$(BASE_BRANCH)`), resolves changed .py files to grimp modules, takes the reverse transitive closure, intersects it with the test-file set, and invokes pytest with only those paths. A conservative fallback list forces the full suite when the changeset includes environment-impacting files, dynamic-import seed modules, non-Python files, an unresolvable baseline, or the canary cadence trips. `make test-all` runs the full suite and, on pass, writes the new LKG sha to `.egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha`. CI switches to `make test-all` so coverage gating is unaffected.

in_scope: Unit-test targets only: the four dirs in `[tool.pytest.ini_options].testpaths` — `tests/`, `gateway/tests/`, `orchestrator/tests/`, `shared/tests/`
`make test-all` = full suite (unconditional) + LKG advance on green
New scripts under `scripts/egg_test_selector/` (or similar) implementing the selection logic
CI workflow `.github/workflows/test.yml` switches `make test` → `make test-all` so the `--cov-fail-under=80` gate still evaluates against the full suite
`docs/guides/testing.md` documenting the new behavior + pointer from `CONTRIBUTING.md` + one-line summary in `make help`
Selection-decision logging: stderr line every invocation + machine-readable record at `.egg-state/selection/<sha>.json`
`--why <test>` introspection surfacing import chain from changed module → selected test
Canary mode: every 10th invocation on a branch falls back to full suite
Unit tests for the selection logic itself (synthetic repo fixture → expected selected set)
out_of_scope: `make test-integration`, `make test-e2e`, `make test-security` — stay full-suite only (Q10)
Pre-commit / lint behavior (issue says 'Pre-commit / lint changes' are out of scope)
pytest-testmon intra-file function narrowing — tracked as a follow-up (Q8)
Performance targets — no hard target for v1; instrument and log metrics, tune in a follow-up issue (Q1)
Merge-commit LKG rewriting — per decision-6 we accept that branches cut from main may inherit a stale-but-valid LKG (sidecar is gitignored so nothing actually leaks to `main`)
Graph cache — keep graph fresh-per-invocation for v1 (can add tree-hash cache later)

success_criteria_mapping.fallback_triggers: Single `FallbackTrigger` enum with a per-enum unit test; integration-level `test_selector_end_to_end.py` asserts full-suite fallback for each trigger.

success_criteria_mapping.test_after_test_all_narrows_vs_lkg: Baseline resolver returns LKG when present and ancestor of HEAD; integration test exercises test-all → edit → test cycle.
success_criteria_mapping.parallel_branches_isolated: Sidecar is keyed by `<branch>` and gitignored → branches never see each other's LKG. Last-writer-wins on same-branch races (Q9) — acceptable.
success_criteria_mapping.merge_lkg_rewrite: N/A under the sidecar model — the file is never checked in, so nothing leaks to main. Explicitly flipped from the issue proposal (decision-6 + decision-9).
success_criteria_mapping.lkg_invalidation_on_trigger_change: Covered by the fallback trigger check running over `git diff $LKG..HEAD` (not just `$LKG...HEAD`) before accepting LKG as the baseline.

decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d1_lkg_update_mechanism: Automatic write to sidecar after every green `make test-all`. `make test-record-good` = manual override.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d2_ci_integration: Switch CI (`.github/workflows/test.yml`) to `make test-all`. `make test` stays the agent/dev fast path.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d3_selection_tool: grimp (static reverse import graph, Rust-backed, `find_downstream_modules(..., as_package=False)`). Adds one dev dep.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d5_non_py_policy_v1: Any non-.py change in the diff → full suite (simple, conservative).
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d6_merge_behavior: Don't rewrite LKG on merge — moot under sidecar (file is gitignored).
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d7_full_suite_target_name: `make test-all` (matches issue language; `make test` becomes changeset-aware).
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d8_gateway_role_policy: Gitignored sidecar sidesteps gateway push policy — no role boundary changes needed.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.d10_dynamic_import_handling: Scan during graph construction — build a `dynamic_import_seeds` set (modules whose source contains `importlib.import_module`, `__import__`, `SourceFileLoader`, or known entry-point registration). Widen to full suite only when a changed module is in that seed set OR (conservatively) when any of those seeds is reachable from a changed module. Default v1: widen when changed ∩ seeds ≠ ∅.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q3_added_triggers: Add `.python-version` to the fallback-trigger allowlist (alongside Makefile, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, workflow file, all conftest.py).
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q4_canary_cadence: Every 10th invocation on a branch forces the full suite. Counter kept at `.egg-state/selection/<branch>.counter`.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q5_pytest_args_interaction: Default: intersect (narrow first, then apply `-k`/path args inside the narrowed set). Explicit path args (anything in `PYTEST_ARGS` that matches `^[a-zA-Z_0-9/.]+\.py(::.*)?$` or starts with a pytest directory) → bypass narrowing entirely (dev override).
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q6_why_flag: Implement `scripts/egg_test_selector/__main__.py --why <test>` printing the import chain `changed_module → ... → test`.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q7_fallback_explain: When falling back, print the specific trigger (`Falling back to full suite: Makefile changed`), not just `Falling back`.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q9_parallel: Last-writer-wins on same-branch LKG races — no coordination.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q11_docs: Create `docs/guides/testing.md`; link from `CONTRIBUTING.md`; add one-line summary to `make help`.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q12_partial_pass: LKG is never updated on a partial-pass run — only `make test-all` (or a `make test` that degraded to full via fallback) writes LKG.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q13_readonly_roles: Read-only agent phases (refiner, reviewer_*) always baseline on `$(BASE_BRANCH)`; they skip the LKG read too (keeps sidecar semantics simple and avoids cross-sandbox staleness).
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q14_bootstrap: Absent sidecar ⇒ no LKG, baseline on base branch. No bootstrap ceremony.
decisions_carried_forward_from_refine.q15_logging: stderr line always + JSON record at `.egg-state/selection/<sha>.json`.

proposed_architecture.overview: One new Python package `scripts/egg_test_selector/` implements baseline resolution, diff collection, grimp graph build, reverse-closure → test-set intersection, fallback triggers, canary counter, logging, and LKG sidecar read/write. The Makefile invokes it as a module (`$(PYTHON) -m egg_test_selector ...`) and feeds its stdout list of test paths to `pytest`.

directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/__main__.py: CLI entry. Subcommands: `select` (default, prints newline-separated test paths), `record-good <sha>` (manual LKG write), `why <test>` (introspection), `selftest` (run `tests/tools/test_selector.py` set). Non-zero exit only on bugs; graceful full-suite fallback is exit 0 plus stderr message.
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/baseline.py: `resolve_baseline(repo: Path, head: str, readonly: bool=False) -> BaselineResult` — returns `(sha, source)` where source ∈ {LKG, BASE_BRANCH}. Order: if readonly → BASE_BRANCH. Else LKG sidecar → validate as 40-char sha + ancestor of HEAD + sha exists in object DB → use it; else BASE_BRANCH (default `origin/main`, overridable via `$BASE_BRANCH`).
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/diff.py: `collect_changed_files(repo, baseline_sha, include_uncommitted=True) -> ChangedFiles` — runs `git diff --name-only <baseline>...HEAD` + `git diff --name-only HEAD` + `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` (untracked).
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/graph.py: `build_graph(repo_root) -> ImportGraph` — wraps `grimp.build_graph(*PACKAGES, include_external_packages=False, exclude_type_checking_imports=True, cache_dir=None)` where PACKAGES is the computed top-level module list (see `packages_for_grimp` section). Also scans every resolvable module for dynamic-import markers and returns `dynamic_import_seeds: set[str]`.
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/selector.py: `select_tests(changed: ChangedFiles, graph: ImportGraph, seeds: set[str]) -> SelectionResult` — resolves each changed .py path to a dotted module name; if any can't be resolved → fallback. Computes `affected = changed ∪ reverse_closure(changed)` where reverse closure is `grimp.find_downstream_modules(m, as_package=False)` unioned over changed modules. If `affected ∩ seeds ≠ ∅` → widen to full (dynamic-import fallback). Intersects `affected` with the set of modules whose file is under the configured test dirs — those are the selected test files.
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/fallback.py: `FallbackTrigger` enum + `check_fallbacks(changed, repo) -> FallbackTrigger | None`. Triggers (in order): EmptyDiff, UnresolvableBaseline, NonPythonChange, ConftestChanged, MakefileChanged, PyprojectChanged, UvLockChanged, PythonVersionChanged, TestWorkflowChanged, DynamicImportSeedChanged, PathUnmappable, LkgNotReachable, CanaryDue.
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/lkg.py: `read_lkg(branch) -> sha | None`, `write_lkg(branch, sha) -> None`, `sidecar_path(branch) -> Path = .egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha`. Branch sanitized for filesystem (slash → `__`). `write_lkg` is the only thing that touches the sidecar; Make recipe calls it via `scripts/egg_test_selector/__main__.py record-good --auto <sha>` from `test-all` on exit 0.
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/canary.py: `bump_and_check(branch) -> bool` — increments `.egg-state/selection/<branch>.counter` atomically (write-then-rename); returns True if the new count % 10 == 0.
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/logging_.py: `log_decision(result: SelectionResult, out_stderr: TextIO, json_path: Path) -> None` — writes human-readable stderr line + JSON file at `.egg-state/selection/<head_sha>.json`.
directory_layout.scripts/egg_test_selector/introspect.py: `why(test_module, changed, graph) -> ImportChain` — for the `--why` CLI; uses `grimp.find_shortest_chain(importer=test_module, imported=changed_module)`.
directory_layout.tests/tools/test_selector_*.py: Per-module unit tests + a `test_selector_end_to_end.py` that builds a synthetic git repo fixture (via `tmp_path` + `subprocess.run(['git', 'init'])`) with a minimal package tree, exercises each code path, and asserts the selected set is exactly what's expected.

proposed_architecture.packages_for_grimp: grimp needs top-level, import-resolvable package names. Given the repo layout + `PYTHONPATH=shared:gateway:orchestrator` and `sys.path.insert` in `tests/conftest.py` pulling in `sandbox/`, the module roster passed to `grimp.build_graph` is computed dynamically: walk the configured source roots (`gateway`, `orchestrator`, `sandbox`, `shared/egg_agent`, `shared/egg_anchor`, `shared/egg_config`, `shared/egg_container`, `shared/egg_contracts`, `shared/egg_git`, `shared/egg_harness`, `shared/egg_harness_integration`, `shared/egg_health`, `shared/egg_logging`, `shared/egg_orchestrator`, `shared/egg_restrictions`, `shared/prompts` if it has .py, `scripts/egg_test_selector`) and each of the four test roots (`tests`, `gateway.tests`, `orchestrator.tests`, `shared.tests`). Edge case: `tests/` is pyproject's root test dir and contains `tests.sandbox.*`, `tests.shared.*`, etc. — those are import-resolvable under the root `tests` package because `tests/__init__.py` exists. The selector has a `PACKAGES` registry in `graph.py` to keep this enumerated in one place, with a smoke test that verifies every `test_*.py` file is reachable in the resulting graph.
proposed_architecture.path_to_module_resolution: `scripts/egg_test_selector/graph.py::resolve_path_to_module(path)` maps `shared/egg_harness/prompt.py` → `egg_harness.prompt`, `gateway/tests/test_gateway.py` → `gateway.tests.test_gateway`, `tests/sandbox/test_orch_client.py` → `tests.sandbox.test_orch_client`. If a changed .py path doesn't resolve under any configured root → `FallbackTrigger.PathUnmappable`.
algorithm: 1. Parse CLI args, load config (PYTEST_ARGS, BASE_BRANCH, role via EGG_AGENT_ROLE).
2. `canary.bump_and_check(branch)` — if due, record CanaryDue trigger for step 9.

3. If explicit path args detected in PYTEST_ARGS → emit 'bypass narrowing (explicit dev override)' and exit 0 with no stdout (Make falls through to full-suite `$PYTEST ... $PYTEST_ARGS`). Note: this path keeps all-test-paths in the Make command so pytest still sees the full testpaths set for -k filtering.
4. Resolve baseline (LKG if present & reachable & role is not read-only; else base branch).
6. Run fallback checks. If triggered → print 'Falling back to full suite: <reason>' on stderr, write JSON record, emit ALL_TEST_PATHS on stdout, exit 0.
8. Resolve changed .py → modules. Any unresolvable → PathUnmappable fallback.
9. Compute reverse closure ∪ self, widen if seeds intersect, intersect with test-files-set.
10. Emit stderr summary + JSON record. Emit selected test paths on stdout (newline separated).
11. Caller (`make test` recipe) pipes stdout into pytest: `TESTS=$$($(PYTHON) -m egg_test_selector select); if [ -z "$$TESTS" ]; then echo 'no tests affected'; exit 0; fi; $(PYTEST) $$TESTS ...`.

make_recipe_shape.test:
Resolve selector output; invoke pytest on that subset; do NOT write LKG. Narrowed behavior:

```
test: export PYTHONPATH := shared:gateway:orchestrator
test: venv
	@echo "==> Selecting tests from changeset..."
	@TESTS=$$($(PYTHON) -m egg_test_selector select) || exit $$?; \
	 if [ -z "$$TESTS" ]; then \
	   echo "No tests affected by changeset."; exit 0; \
	 fi; \
	 $(PYTEST) $$TESTS -v -m "not functional" $(PYTEST_ARGS)
```
make_recipe_shape.test-all:
Run the full suite unconditionally; on pass (exit 0) advance LKG via the selector CLI:

```
test-all: export PYTHONPATH := shared:gateway:orchestrator
test-all: venv
	@echo "==> Running full unit-test suite..."
	$(PYTEST) tests/ gateway/tests/ orchestrator/tests/ shared/tests/ -v -m "not functional" $(PYTEST_ARGS) && \
	 $(PYTHON) -m egg_test_selector record-good --auto $$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```
make_recipe_shape.test-record-good:
Explicit one-liner:

```
test-record-good:
	$(PYTHON) -m egg_test_selector record-good $$(git rev-parse HEAD)
```

proposed_architecture.ci_changes: .github/workflows/test.yml: change `make test PYTEST_ARGS="..."` → `make test-all PYTEST_ARGS="--cov=gateway --cov=shared --cov=sandbox --cov-report=term-missing --cov-fail-under=80"`. No checkout depth changes required (decision-11).
proposed_architecture.gitignore_changes: Append `.egg-state/last-known-good/`, `.egg-state/selection/` to .gitignore so the sidecar + selection logs + canary counter never enter git history. Explicit per the refine-phase sidecar decision (decision-9 + decision-8).
proposed_architecture.dependency_addition: Add `grimp>=3.14,<4.0` to `[project.optional-dependencies].dev` in pyproject.toml. grimp 3.x is the current stable (Dec 2025 release), Rust-backed, and `find_downstream_modules(..., as_package=False)` is a stable public API.
proposed_architecture.role_awareness: The selector consults `EGG_AGENT_ROLE` env var (set by the sandbox). For read-only roles (refiner, reviewer_*) it always uses base-branch baseline and skips both LKG reads and LKG writes. For other roles LKG is the preferred baseline.

logging_format.stderr_example: egg-test-selector: baseline=LKG(6cc0bf4) diff=4 files selected=12 tests full_suite=no fallback=none time=140ms
logging_format.stderr_fallback_example: egg-test-selector: baseline=BASE_BRANCH(origin/main) diff=57 files FALLBACK → full suite (reason=ConftestChanged path=gateway/tests/conftest.py)
logging_format.retention: Selection JSON lives at `.egg-state/selection/<sha>.json` — last-writer-wins per HEAD sha; no pruning (gitignored). Stale ones accumulate only on the dev's working tree; rm -rf is the recovery.

alternatives_considered.name: Approach A (chosen): grimp reverse import graph + sidecar LKG
alternatives_considered.description: Static grimp graph, reverse closure, gitignored per-branch sidecar. No prior test run needed; deterministic and explainable.
pros: Zero runtime state to seed — graph is fresh per invocation (Rust-backed grimp is fast enough; ~1s on repos this size)
Clean merge/rebase semantics: sidecar is gitignored, so main history is untouched
Explainable via `--why` (grimp exposes find_shortest_chain out of the box)
Handles shared/ → gateway/+orchestrator/+sandbox/ cross-package fan-out naturally
cons: Blind to dynamic imports (mitigated by seed-set widen + conservative fallback)
No intra-file narrowing — selects whole test files not individual test functions (follow-up: pytest-testmon)
grimp requires all imported modules to be resolvable; mixed-package layout forces us to maintain the PACKAGES enumeration

alternatives_considered.name: Approach B: pytest-testmon coverage-based selection
alternatives_considered.description: Instrument one full run with pytest-testmon; it records per-test coverage into `.testmondata`. Subsequent runs select tests whose coverage overlaps the diff.
pros: Catches dynamic imports along executed paths
cons: Requires a prior full run to seed `.testmondata`; bootstrap pain
Known rough edges with pytest-cov (our CI runs with --cov); has historically produced stale selections
The `.testmondata` file is a large binary artifact — awkward for sidecar/sandbox semantics
Harder to explain when a test is selected (no shortest-chain equivalent)
alternatives_considered.rationale_for_rejection: Decision-3 already picked grimp. testmon stays a follow-up option (Q8).

alternatives_considered.name: Approach C: Hand-curated dir → dir mapping (Airflow-style)
alternatives_considered.description: Maintain a YAML map: `changes under gateway/policy.py → run gateway/tests/`. Zero graph dep; zero dynamic import risk.
cons: Coarse: would select whole gateway/tests/ for a one-liner in policy.py — fails the leaf-module acceptance criterion explicitly
Breaks silently when someone adds a new import
alternatives_considered.rationale_for_rejection: Does not meet the 'leaf module → just the tests that import it' acceptance criterion (decision-3).

alternatives_considered.name: Approach D: hand-rolled ast-based reverse graph
alternatives_considered.description: Write the ~300-line reverse-closure algorithm ourselves using stdlib `ast`.
cons: Reimplements grimp — including namespace-package handling, relative imports, TYPE_CHECKING guard skipping
More code to maintain; fewer eyes on edge cases
alternatives_considered.rationale_for_rejection: Decision-3 picked grimp. 'Don't write what you can `uv add`'.

modified_files: CONTRIBUTING.md (link to docs/guides/testing.md; update `make test` description)
untouched: gateway/**, orchestrator/**, sandbox/**, shared/** (source code untouched)

git_assumptions: `origin/main` reachable locally when using base-branch baseline. In CI this is moot because CI uses `make test-all`; for local/sandbox the sandbox has origin/main fetched (it's the default BASE_BRANCH).
`git rev-parse HEAD`, `git merge-base`, `git cat-file -e <sha>` all work in the agent sandbox.
filesystem_assumptions: `.egg-state/` is writable by the role (it already is — agents write drafts/reviews here).
`.egg-state/last-known-good/`, `.egg-state/selection/` directories auto-created by the selector (os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True)).
constraints_and_dependencies.gateway_policy: None. Sidecar is gitignored so never pushed; no role-boundary changes required. Selector scripts live under `scripts/egg_test_selector/` which is writable by coder (and any other role that modifies scripts).
constraints_and_dependencies.sandbox_compat: Selector must run under the sandbox's Python. It uses stdlib + grimp only; no dependency on orchestrator/gateway runtime.
constraints_and_dependencies.interaction_with_cov: `make test` invocations that pass `PYTEST_ARGS='--cov=...'` will now compute coverage against a subset of the suite — that subset's coverage will legitimately be < 80%. The fix is already built into the plan: CI uses `make test-all` (decision-2). Local devs who want coverage should run `make test-all` explicitly; we document this in docs/guides/testing.md.
constraints_and_dependencies.read_only_roles: refiner + reviewer_* have `.egg-readonly` markers; selector detects EGG_AGENT_ROLE and falls back to base-branch baseline unconditionally for those roles (never reads LKG — keeps the sidecar a write-from-test-all-only artifact).

risks_to_hand_to_risk_analyst: grimp fails to resolve some internal module (e.g., `shared/prompts` is not a proper Python package) → selection aborts. Mitigation: smoke-test in the selector's own unit tests that every test_*.py file is present in the graph.

Dynamic-import blind spot: plugin-registry modules that use `importlib.import_module` at runtime could be silently missed if their changed source isn't in the seed set AND the seed sweep doesn't catch the registration pattern. Mitigation: canary fallback every 10th run + conservative widen on seed-set-reachable diffs. Residual risk: a rare silent miss. Instrumented by JSON logs so we can post-mortem.

Slow selector startup: grimp rebuilds the graph per invocation. On the current repo (~770 .py files) this should be sub-second, but worth measuring. If it becomes a problem, add a tree-hash-keyed cache in a follow-up.
LKG sidecar race (two agents on same branch): last-writer-wins. Risk is benign (both are green shas) but could cause counter-intuitive baselining. Q9 accepted this explicitly.
Branch name with slashes (`egg/issue-1973-architect/work`) must map to a filesystem-safe sidecar name — escape `/` → `__`. Tested in test_selector_lkg.py.

PATH resolution for `$(PYTHON) -m egg_test_selector` requires `scripts/` to be on PYTHONPATH during `make test`. Because the Makefile already sets `PYTHONPATH := shared:gateway:orchestrator` on the test target, we extend it to include `scripts` too, OR install the selector as a script entry point via `pyproject.toml [project.scripts]`. Plan: add `scripts` to the existing PYTHONPATH line in the Makefile — simplest and consistent with how other scripts are invoked.

CI aggregate action: the `Test` workflow has three jobs (unit, security, aggregate). Changing `unit` to `make test-all` is orthogonal to `aggregate` — aggregate just reads `needs.unit.result`, so no impact.

Developer confusion if `make test` reports 'No tests affected' after a refactor that only touches whitespace — the stderr summary + `--why` affordance are the explicit mitigations. Worth calling out in docs/guides/testing.md.

Breakage in the test target itself while this feature is in flight: if `egg_test_selector` raises an unhandled exception, `make test` fails closed. Plan: wrap the CLI with a blanket try/except that logs the exception to stderr AND exits 0 with full-suite fallback. This means bugs in the selector never block development; the stderr message makes them visible.

`make test-all` wraps pytest with `&& record-good`. If pytest exits non-zero the LKG is not written (correct). If pytest exits 0 but record-good fails (e.g. .egg-state not writable), the test suite exit code is the OR of both — `make` will report failure even though tests passed. Acceptable: surfaces real problems; fix by fixing the environment.

acceptance_criteria_proposal: `make test` invoked on a branch that changed only `gateway/policy.py` selects only tests whose transitive reverse closure includes `gateway.policy` (per the synthetic-repo fixture, this is provably a strict subset of `gateway/tests/`).

`make test` invoked on a branch that changed a module in `shared/egg_harness/` selects tests from `gateway/tests/`, `orchestrator/tests/`, `shared/tests/` — wherever `egg_harness` is transitively imported.

Editing any of: Makefile, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, .python-version, .github/workflows/test.yml, any conftest.py, any dynamic-import seed module → stderr prints `Falling back to full suite: <specific trigger>` and runs the full suite.
`make test-all` always runs the full suite and — on exit 0 — writes `.egg-state/last-known-good/<branch>.sha` containing a 40-char sha matching `git rev-parse HEAD`.
`make test` after a successful `make test-all` + one-file edit uses LKG as the baseline (verified via stderr log line containing `baseline=LKG(<sha>)`) and selects only affected tests.

Two branches iterating in parallel on the same clone each have their own sidecar file and never interfere (verified in end-to-end test by creating two branches, running test-all on each, checking both sidecars exist independently).
LKG that points to a sha not reachable from HEAD (simulated by rebasing past it) → `Falling back to full suite: LkgNotReachable` on next `make test`.
LKG is invalidated (fallback to full suite + LKG not used as baseline this run) when a fallback-trigger file changed between LKG sha and HEAD.
`tests/tools/test_selector_*.py` exists and exercises each module + a synthetic-repo end-to-end scenario for all acceptance criteria.
`docs/guides/testing.md` exists; `CONTRIBUTING.md` links to it; `make help` mentions `make test-all` + `make test-record-good`.
CI workflow runs `make test-all` with the `--cov-fail-under=80` gate intact.
Every `make test` invocation writes `.egg-state/selection/<head-sha>.json` with the schema defined in `logging_format.json_schema`.
`make test PYTEST_ARGS='tests/test_python_syntax.py'` (explicit path in PYTEST_ARGS) bypasses narrowing — pytest sees the full testpaths set + user's -k/-path args, as it does today.

`.venv/bin/python -m egg_test_selector why tests/sandbox/test_output.py` prints a human-readable import chain when that test is currently in the selection set; prints a clear 'not selected' message otherwise.
Every 10th `make test` invocation on a given branch falls back to the full suite (stderr: `Falling back to full suite: CanaryDue`).
Selection JSON schema is stable across v1 (documented in `docs/guides/testing.md`) — downstream tooling can rely on it.
Read-only agent roles (refiner, reviewer_*) ignore LKG and always baseline on `$(BASE_BRANCH)`.
Selector exception-handles: a bug in the selector prints the traceback to stderr and falls back to full suite (exit code 0 from the selector; `make test` continues).
